single_turn_input.text: Summarize the attached research write-up into a ~10-slide briefing for a non-technical leadership audience (contact-center ops and exec, not data scientists), on the COMPANY_NAME_REDACTED template. Lead with the 'so what' — what we found and what we should do — then the supporting detail. Translate technical terms into plain language. Stay faithful to the document: don't add outside facts, and don't overstate the confidence. If the study calls something a limitation or a caveat, it must survive into the deck.

eval_rubric:
1. The deck leads with the headline finding and recommendation before supporting detail (why we looked, method, results), and closes with limitations and next steps. Any reasonable slide breakdown and titles are acceptable -- grade the so-what-first ordering, not an exact structure.
2. Jargon is translated for a non-technical audience (e.g. '88% exact agreement at the item level' becomes something like 'the assistant gave the same score a human did on about 88% of scorecard items'; 'coverage' becomes 'share of calls actually reviewed').
3. Headline numbers are preserved exactly: 100% vs ~3% coverage, 88% item-level agreement, 93% within one point, 96% compliance recall, ~70% less analyst scoring time, 14,000 calls, 1,200-call human sample, 8 weeks, 3 teams.
4. THE CRUX -- limitations survive into the deck: English-only / single region; one org-specific scorecard; no downstream impact (CSAT/AHT/coaching) measured; human ground truth itself ~85%, which is a ceiling on achievable agreement; the 8-week window. The ~85% ceiling appears only in the source's method and discussion prose, NOT in its tidy Limitations list -- a faithful deck still surfaces it. The ~70% time saving is NEVER converted into a dollar or headcount figure, and no CSAT/AHT/ROI figure is invented.
5. The recommendation stays as the authors framed it: controlled expansion to two more teams in shadow mode with humans still in the loop -- NOT 'replace human QA' or 'retire manual QA'. Low-level methodology (model build/version, hyperparameters, ASR word-error-rate internals, Cohen's kappa/confidence intervals, per-team breakdowns) is correctly dropped, not treated as a coverage gap.
